SPECTRAL TRANSVERSALITY SOURCE AUDIT
2026-10-08. Assigned scope: area restoration and Lemmas 2.1/2.2 only.

VERDICT

I independently reconstruct the source's two-direction splitting and finite-
cutoff path avoidance arguments. I find no fatal gap in these two lemmas.
The proof also gives the relative C^r density needed for finite-stage smooth
path perturbations, with the compatibility assumptions stated below.

This is an internal mathematical reconstruction, conditional only on standard
elliptic regularity, scalar unique continuation, finite-dimensional implicit
function theory, and elementary measure-zero facts. Scalar unique continuation
was checked in the original Aronszajn--Krzywicki--Szarski paper. The Moser
construction was reconstructed explicitly and checked against the original
Moser proof. There is no formal proof or external expert validation here.

There are three material scope limits:

1. The valid surjectivity is onto the TWO TRACELESS ENTRIES on any real
   orthonormal eigenfunction pair. It is not arbitrary full-matrix surjectivity
   for a high-multiplicity eigenspace, nor simultaneous independent control
   of every cluster. In particular, area-normalized conformal perturbations
   of a whole round-sphere degree-l block have zero trace at first order.
2. The even-family conclusion concerns simplicity separately within the even
   and odd spectral lists. Cross-parity coincidences are explicitly allowed.
3. Relative data that are required to remain simple must already be simple.
   Endpoints with a repeated eigenvalue cannot be fixed while demanding
   simplicity there. Intentional crossing neighborhoods can be frozen only
   if they are exempted and already contain no unwanted coincidence.

No cross-block crossing existence (Lemma 2.5), exact-double preservation
(Lemma 2.3), radial transfer, curvature realization, or common-metric argument
was audited in this assignment. No bound uniform in the spectral cutoff is
obtained by this audit.

EXACT-DOUBLE SPECTRAL AUDIT
2026-10-08. Assigned scope: OpenAI family 361, Lemma 2.3 and the extra
all-spectrum, crossing-jet, and fixed-area interface needed by a countable library.

VERDICT

I reconstructed Lemma 2.3 and found no counterexample or missing hypothesis in
its stated finite-cutoff claim. The key fact is weaker than full Strong Arnold
transversality: every unwanted positive repeated eigenspace admits SOME nonscalar
first variation inside the two tangent constraints retaining the designated
double. Its proof by equal product spans, equal nodal sets, and a nodal-domain
energy test is sound in this real scalar, connected, smooth surface setting.

The paper proves a finite-q conclusion, not an all-spectrum one. The additional
countable interface can nevertheless be reconstructed, with the explicit Baire
spaces and endpoint qualifications below. In particular, a single exact-double
metric can have every other eigenvalue simple, and a smooth curve through it can
have no other repetition anywhere while retaining its value and prescribed
nonzero first derivative. These are internal existence proofs, not external
validation of the manuscript, quantitative algorithms, or novelty findings.

Dependence on Lemma 2.2 is limited to its actual small finite-pool perturbation
argument for a compact path, rather than bare existence of some joining path.
The distinct assigned audit of Lemmas 2.1-2.2 remains relevant to that premise.

INDEPENDENT CROSS-BLOCK AUDIT: OPENAI FAMILY 361, LEMMA 2.5
2026-10-08. Bounded reconstruction. No descendants, publication, push, or edits to other workers' files.

VERDICT

The full initial-double generation of Lemma 2.5 is internally reconstructed: both the within-round-block harmonic-product/submersion argument and the cross-block quantitative mechanism. Lemma 2.4's pole-regular Wronskian and parity claims are reconstructed too. No fatal error was found in the sector min-max estimates, parity counts, pole conditions, area normalization, or the exact Liouville conjugation. In fact the source's o(l) inversion remainder can be strengthened to O(1), uniformly in the degree and in the deformation parameter. This yields an inversion of size at least 0.7*l-O(1).

Obtaining an isolated EXACT DOUBLE at the desired combined-spectrum positions remains conditional on the finite-cutoff statements of source Lemmas 2.1-2.3, which are assigned to other auditors. This audit checks the precise interfaces required from them, without substituting their conclusions for independently established external theorems. A nonzero first-order crossing follows locally from Lemma 2.1 after the exact double is isolated. Its slope and neighborhood radius may depend arbitrarily on the degree and cutoff.

There is no need for a uniform-in-degree inverse-function radius in the source's actual finite-per-degree construction. Arbitrarily small corrections in a prescribed finite C^r norm suffice. A common positive crossing slope, common phase width, common Riesz-frame derivative bound, or uniform IFT inverse across all degrees is NOT established here. These stronger conclusions must not be inferred from Lemma 2.5 or Proposition 3.1.
